column1: # First real MySQL TCP connection source evidence.

column5: One serial real TcpStream lifecycle performs the initial handshake, bounded root empty-password admission, COM_PING, COM_QUERY, COM_QUIT, incremental result or ERR writing, protocol sequence reset, peer-close isolation, and exactly-once cleanup. TLS, compression on the live socket, prepared statements, public authentication, kill state, metrics, deadlines, and concurrent connection execution remain open.

The existing TCP bind/listener authority now accepts and completely serves one serial MySQL connection through an injected query engine with connection accounting. Unix sockets, PROXY protocol, status HTTP, graceful process shutdown, admission controls, and concurrent serving remain open.
